body: Running a rental portfolio in Gainesville means making constant decisions about security, cost, and timing. Lock rekeying at scale is one of the smartest ways to protect your units between tenants without replacing hardware that still has years of life left. Whether you oversee a few homes near Haile Plantation or a larger complex on the northwest side of town, understanding how volume rekeying works will help you plan better and protect your investment.
Why Lock Rekeying at Scale Matters More Than You Might Think

Every time a tenant moves out, you lose control of who holds a key to that unit. Keys get copied, shared with guests, or simply not returned. Full lock replacement on every unit is expensive and often unnecessary when the hardware is still in good condition. Rekeying changes the internal pin configuration of the lock cylinder so that old keys no longer work, giving you a clean slate for the new tenant at a fraction of the cost.

For property managers handling multiple units, the savings add up quickly. You protect your tenants, your property, and your liability exposure without swapping out hardware that does not need replacing.
What Does the Rekeying Process Look Like Across Multiple Units?

A qualified mobile locksmith can service multiple units in a single visit, working through each door in order. The technician removes the lock cylinder, replaces the key pins to match a new cut, reassembles the hardware, and confirms the lock functions correctly before moving on. If any lock is worn or binding, you get a real-time report on that hardware rather than a surprise call from a new tenant on move-in day.
Preparation on your end makes the job move faster. Before the appointment, have the following ready:

• A complete list of unit numbers to be rekeyed
  • Notes on any locks that may need repair rather than a simple rekey
  • Information on lock types or any non-standard hardware
  • Access coordination for occupied or partially vacated units
Should You Consider a Master Key System for Your Property?

If you manage multiple units in the same building or complex, a master key system can eliminate the need to carry a separate key for every door. Each tenant's key opens only their unit, while a single master key provides access to all units for maintenance and emergencies. This structure is especially useful when you also need to give limited access to contractors.

The system requires planning upfront but saves significant time and reduces access errors across a large portfolio. A locksmith experienced in property access can design and install the system in a single coordinated visit.
How Do You Time Rekeying Into Your Turnover Schedule?

The most efficient approach is to schedule your rekey appointment during the window between a tenant's move-out inspection and the next tenant's move-in date. For properties with staggered lease endings, many managers find it more efficient to batch rekeying appointments by property cluster rather than scheduling a separate visit for each unit. Our property management locksmith service in Gainesville is designed to accommodate this kind of volume scheduling. New lock installations needed due to hardware damage from the previous tenancy can often be handled in the same visit.
What About IC Core Locks for High-Turnover Properties?

For properties with very high turnover, such as student housing near the University of Florida, interchangeable core locks offer a faster solution. These systems let you swap out the entire lock core in seconds using a control key, with no tools and no locksmith required on-site for every change. You keep a set of pre-keyed cores and rotate them as tenants turn over.
The upfront cost is higher than standard residential locks, but the long-term labor savings can be significant for units that turn over frequently throughout the year.
Keeping Access Control Consistent Across Your Portfolio

One area property managers often overlook is key control documentation. Keeping clear records of which keys were issued, which locks have been rekeyed and when, and which properties are on a master key system prevents access gaps that can create real problems later. This becomes especially important when maintenance staff or contractors change.
Pairing your rekeying program with periodic service for shared access points covers your entire portfolio:

• Leasing offices and common entry doors
  • Mail rooms and package areas
  • Maintenance storage and utility rooms
  • Exterior gate locks and side entrances

A coordinated approach keeps everything current and reduces the risk of access that should have been removed.
